subject: Post-call recap: deterministic JSON output & agent wiring (Ava Retail)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@avaretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: deterministic JSON output & agent wiring (Ava Retail)

Maya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and to capture next steps. I’ve CC'd Grace who will support the POC and Elli (internal) for infra/ops questions.

Pain points you shared:
- Current chatbot returns free-form product info that the commerce backend struggles to parse (orders, SKUs).
- Compliance requires auditable, schema-validated outputs for downstream systems.
- Intermittent latency spikes during promotions; need predictable low tail latency for query-to-action flows.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Frontend: React storefront calling a Node microservice (order orchestration).
- LLM usage today: hosted model via vendor X (no structured output guarantees).
- Backend: Postgres + custom event router for fulfillment.

Success criteria for an initial POC (as discussed):
1) Deterministic JSON responses for 95% of queries that map to fulfillment actions (fields strict-validated against JSON Schema).
2) Median latency < 250ms and p95 < 800ms for single-turn queries under test load.
3) Ability to route ambiguous queries to a human handoff flow with one-click audit trail.

Functional ask we discussed (tool/function calling + structured output):
- We’ll provide an explicit JSON Schema for the fulfillment action payload (required fields, enums for SKUs/actions).
- Redwood runtime will validate model output against the schema; failures will be surfaced as structured error objects rather than free text.
- Support agent-style workflows: chain-of-tools where the model can call a ‘price_check’ tool, then an ‘inventory_query’, then emit a final validated payload.

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Rishi: Send initial spec & example prompt set (attached) — today (attachment: ava-mvp-prompt-set.json).
- Grace: Draft POC success test harness (latency and schema validation tests) — EOD Thu 3/12.
- Maya: Share 2 anonymized example user queries and the current orchestration contract for the order service — by EOD Wed 3/11.

Attachments included: Redwood agent wiring brief (redwood-agent-specs.pdf) and the prompt set.

If that matches your view, we’ll schedule a 30-min technical sync with your platform engineer and our runtime team (suggest Fri 3/13 10:00-10:30 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@avaretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deterministic JSON output & agent wiring (Ava Retail)

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful and accurate. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The SKU enum will be fairly large (we can provide a service endpoint that returns valid SKUs — prefer that over a static enum if your runtime can call a tool to fetch it).
- For auditable outputs, we need the ability to persist the model's canonical payload + the validation result (pass/fail + diff) into our event log.
- Human handoff: when the model is > 70% uncertain we want an explicit flag in the payload so our UI can surface the case.

We’ll upload 3 representative queries and the orchestration contract by EOD today. Fri 10am PT works for the tech sync.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maya
Senior Product Manager, Platform | Ava Retail
maya.singh@avaretail.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft POC test plan for Ava Retail (schema & tooling)

Quick internal note before the tech sync — summary of what I’ll prepare: 

- Test harness outline:
  * Schema validation tests (positive/negative cases using the example queries).
  * Tool-call integration tests: mock SKU endpoint and inventory endpoint; assert model calls sequence.
  * Performance tests: single-client latency profile + synthetic traffic for promo-like burst.
- Success thresholds to present: median <250ms, p95 <800ms, schema pass >=95%.
- Error handling behavior proposal: return a structured error object {"validation_error": {"field":"price","reason":"missing"}} and include original model text in a separate audit field.

Attachments I’ll include in the sync: redwood-agent-specs.pdf (wiring diagrams) and a short checklist for ops to capture logs.

I’ll also draft the initial Postman collection to simulate the frontend flow.

Grace
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
